articles.title: UUIDv7 doesn't have the properties you think it does
articles.summary: UUIDv7 is built on shards of silicon, and its properties are not as straightforward as claimed. Most blog posts about UUIDv7 tout its benefits, but certain implementations violate these properties to extreme degrees. The only useful property UUIDv7 appears to strictly provide is uniqueness, and it can be used for collision resistance, but the timestamp embedded in the ID may not relate to the object creation time. This can lead to inaccuracies, particularly in scenarios where the difference between the timestamp and the current time can be arbitrarily large.

articles.title: Software is slow because of bad design, not slow languages
articles.summary: Software performance is not solely determined by the language used, but rather by the design of the program itself. While some languages, such as C, can be significantly faster than others, such as Python, rewriting a Python program in C will not result in a significant speedup. Instead, most slow languages already have popular libraries that allow them to unlock C-like speed. In general, performance is a matter of design, not of language choice, and most real programs are I/O-bound, meaning they spend most of their time waiting for data to be input or output.

However, lean-zip was unable to match the performance of libdeflate, a C implementation, which was able to outperform the library in certain benchmarks. This suggests that lean-zip is not yet close to achieving pure functional programming language performance, but rather is a stepping stone towards achieving that goal.

This binary is particularly interesting because it provides a way to dynamically select the compiler based on the tool name, which can be useful in certain development scenarios.
